title: Noether Symmetries Generate Deterministic Energy-Harvesting Protocols
authors: Ali Akil, M. Hamed Mohammady, Zihan Wang, Oscar Dahlsten
abstract: We consider the general principles for when deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is possible. DEH means absorbing energy from a fluctuating source without entropy being absorbed. We show that the symmetry structure of the source--harvester dynamics gives a general route beyond existing examples to identify DEH capable source states. Any continuous symmetry with a conserved Noether charge induces a source-side orbit of states that all implement the same deterministic harvester transition, provided the harvester boundary states are symmetry invariant. Consequently, one DEH capable source state with nonzero asymmetry between charge sectors can generate infinitely many simultaneously DEH capable source states. A Jaynes-Cummings model, a three-spin XX chain, and an SU(2) model illustrate the construction. We further extend Noether's theorem to generalised probabilistic theories and thereby generalise our main result. We further establish an asymmetry bound for harvesting, showing that source asymmetry cannot increase on average, while DEH saturates the bound exactly preserving asymmetry.
summary: This paper develops a general theory showing that deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is governed by the symmetries of the source-harvester system. By applying Noether's theorem, the authors prove that a single symmetry can generate an infinite family of source states, all capable of performing the exact same energy transfer. This establishes a fundamental, symmetry-protected principle for quantum energy extraction.
main_problem: The paper seeks to determine the general theoretical conditions under which deterministic energy harvesting (DEH) is possible from fluctuating quantum sources.
main_result: It establishes that Noether's theorem provides a general principle: a continuous symmetry of the joint source-harvester dynamics guarantees that an entire orbit of source states can perform the same deterministic energy transfer.
method: The authors employ Noether's theorem to link continuous symmetries (and conserved charges) to the existence of multiple source states that yield identical, deterministic energy transfer outcomes on the harvester.
model_or_system: The system involves a coupled quantum source and harvester described by a Hamiltonian $H = H_h + H_s + H_{int}$. The analysis is generalized to include classical and phase-space dynamics.
key_observables: Deterministic energy transfer ($ho_i^h 	o ho_f^h$), source asymmetry ($I(\sigma)$), and the conserved Noether charges ($Q_\alpha$).

main_assumptions: The primary assumptions for the main theorem are the existence of an exact Noether symmetry for the joint dynamics and the exact invariance of the harvester boundary states under this symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how Noether symmetry generates orbits of source states that jointly achieve DEH, and show population dynamics for non-Abelian DEH protocols.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining DEH and identifying the role of symmetries, proving the main theorem using Noether's theorem, illustrating the concept with specific models (Jaynes-Cummings, XX chain), and finally generalizing the findings to other physical theories.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, fundamental constraint (symmetry protection) on non-equilibrium quantum processes like energy harvesting, connecting deep mathematical principles (Noether's theorem) to practical quantum engineering problems.
